text:
anya: quick question — compliance flagged a gap: when a customer deletes their BYOK (customer-managed key) we currently keep audit events for 90d, but legal wants immutable evidence for 2 years. is there a technical blocker to extending retention for only the BYOK audit stream? :thinking:

mike: interesting. which events do they want preserved? key-create/key-import/key-schedule-delete/key-usage/rewrap?
sarah: they explicitly called out import, delete, rewrap, and operator-escrow actions. they want chain-of-custody logs for any key lifecycle op.

anya: yes — import, attestation, delete, rewrap, and any HSM operator actions (manual unseal/escrow). also need proof that we removed key material from ephemeral stores after delete.
jordan: two constraints I can think of off the top: 1) our current audit pipeline aggregates and then TTLs at the index level (ELK/GCS export). extending retention for a subset means either tagging and routing to a separate index/bucket or adding retention metadata to objects. 2) BYOK customers sometimes require we delete derived telemetry on request (data minimization) — conflicting ask.

anya: good call on the minimization conflict. legal said they can sign an exception if we isolate BYOK audit events in an immutable store (WORM) with access controls. they asked for a proposal + timelines.
mike: proposal sketch: route BYOK lifecycle events to a dedicated audit bucket with object versioning + lock (e.g., GCS retention policy or S3 Object Lock). encrypt that bucket with a different CMK (company-managed) and restrict who can list/get. add an attestation document on deletion flow.
sarah: we also need RBAC changes: only sec-audit and legal-sig roles can read that bucket, and reads should be logged to a separate read-audit stream (no one gets on-demand dumps). also require multi-person approval for any export.
jordan: operational details: how do we ensure events still land there if the KMS itself is being decommissioned or during HSM maintenance windows? we need write-through/queueing if audit service is unavailable.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline note: currently event router has a single topic `kms-lifecycle-events` — adding conditional split based on `event.key_origin == BYOK` is a safe change but needs end-to-end tests and a backfill plan.

anya: backfill — legal wants historical evidence for the past 18 months for a small subset of customers. do we have the data to backfill or will we need to request customer attestations?
mike: we keep raw event blobs for 1 year in cold storage, and parsed indices for 90d. so 18 months partially available. backfill plan: 1) rehydrate cold blobs -> filter BYOK -> put into WORM bucket; 2) run integrity checks and produce a hash chain file per customer.
sarah: hash chain is good. also add a signed timestamp from two engineers to prove non-repudiation at the time of export.
jordan: vulnerability angle: if we extend retention we increase blast radius for exfiltration. we should scope access via VPC-SC, vault-derived ephemeral creds for audit readers, and require hardware-enforced MFA on export.

anya: noted. can we add MFA + require ephemeral sessions for any direct read of WORM bucket?
mike: yes — short-lived signed URLs for internal tooling + ephemeral STS tokens. exports must be gated by a canary job that verifies integrity before anyone can download.
oncall-bot: reminder: oncall rotation may be paged for any write-failures to the new audit sink during initial rollout (severity: high).

sarah: action items I hear: 1) design doc for WORM BYOK audit sink (owner: mike) 2) RBAC proposal and iam policy snippets (owner: sarah) 3) backfill plan and hash-chain tooling (owner: jordan) 4) threat model & export controls (owner: anya). please add timelines.

anya: timeline proposal: design doc + threat model in 1 week, PoC routing change and small WORM bucket in 3 weeks, backfill run for initial customer set in 5 weeks. can we commit?
mike: I can get the design doc + PoC work, 3-week PoC looks tight but doable if infra helps with test buckets.
jordan: I'll own the hash-chain tooling and backfill scripts. 5 weeks sounds ok for a pilot subset (5 customers).
sarah: I'll draft IAM policy snippets and an RBAC playbook for audits + export SOP.

anya: compliance asked also about forensic readiness: they want a playbook for incident response when a BYOK event is suspicious (e.g., unauthorized rewrap). we need runbooks that call on oncall, legal, and the HSM vendor.
mike: propose a short runbook stub in the design doc with steps: 1) freeze exports & snapshot WORM bucket 2) notify legal + create legal hold 3) collect volatile logs (host, usb, operator session) 4) engage HSM vendor for firmware/firmware logs 5) preserve chain-of-custody.

jordan: add a fallback: if customer requests immediate key destruction, we require a signed request and then mark the WORM bucket entry with deletion-request metadata; actual audit retention window per legal exception will be documented.

anya: OK — I'll prepare an executive summary for legal and compliance. please post PRs to the `infra-audit-routing` repo and tag me. :thumbsup:

mike: ack, creating issue and will ping infra for service account quota for test bucket.
sarah: ack, I'll start IAM draft and post in this thread when ready.

jordan: starting hash-chain prototype, will include sample verification CLI:
```
# verify tool example
verify-byok-audit --bucket gs://redwood-byo-worm --customer-id cust-123 
# output: 2026-07-14T12:34:56Z OK hashchain-valid signer:alice,signer:bob
```

anya: thanks all. filing this as action items in the security board. will follow up with timelines in 24h. :eyes:
